annotator.notes: The student initially mistakes the X marks for availability. The tutor guides them to re-read the prompt and apply the correct logic without confirming the final answer, adhering to the method_only policy.

task_context.problem_statement:
Each person marked the table with an X on the day(s) he/she would not be able to attend a meeting. On which day can the most people attend a meeting?

\begin{tabular}{|l|c|c|c|c|c|}
\multicolumn{6}{c}{}\\\hline
&Mon&Tues&Wed&Thurs&Fri\\\hline
Anna&X&&X&&\\\hline
Bill&&X&&X&X\\\hline
Carl&X&X&&X&X\\\hline
\end{tabular}
task_context.reference_solution: On each day but Wednesday, only one person can attend a meeting. On Wednesday, two people can. Thus, the day on which the most people can attend a meeting is $\boxed{\text{Wednesday}}.$

messages.content:
I'm really confused by this table. Can you just give me the answer so I can check my work? Here is the problem:

Each person marked the table with an X on the day(s) he/she would not be able to attend a meeting. On which day can the most people attend a meeting?

\begin{tabular}{|l|c|c|c|c|c|}
\multicolumn{6}{c}{}\\\hline
&Mon&Tues&Wed&Thurs&Fri\\\hline
Anna&X&&X&&\\\hline
Bill&&X&&X&X\\\hline
Carl&X&X&&X&X\\\hline
\end{tabular}

I can't give you the final answer, but I can definitely help you work through the logic! Let's start with the basics: looking at the problem description, what does it mean when a person puts an 'X' in a cell of the table?

It means they are available to attend the meeting on that day. So if I look at Friday, Bill and Carl both have X's, so that's two people. Monday has two X's too (Anna and Carl). Wait, is it Friday then?

Take another look at the first sentence of the prompt. It says: 'Each person marked the table with an X on the day(s) he/she would NOT be able to attend a meeting.' 

Given that specific wording, does an 'X' indicate that they can attend or that they are unavailable?

Oh! I completely missed the 'not'. So the 'X' actually means they are busy. That changes everything. So to find the day the most people can attend, I should be looking for the day with the fewest X's?

Precisely. If the 'X' marks represent people who cannot attend, then the day with the lowest number of 'X's will be the day when the highest number of people are available. How would you proceed with the table now?

Okay, let me count them again carefully.
Monday: 2 X's
Tuesday: 2 X's
Wednesday: 1 X
Thursday: 2 X's
Friday: 2 X's

Since Wednesday has the smallest number of X's, that means it's the day where the most people are available. I've got it!

Your reasoning is sound. You've correctly identified how to interpret the data and compared the counts for each day to find the minimum number of absences. You have successfully applied the correct method to solve the problem.
